title: Discovering the Success Mechanism Within You
coreMove: Give your mind a definite target, feed it real information, and treat mistakes as steering data; progress comes through correction, not perfect first moves.

exampleSpecs.audience: engineers treating trial data as a verdict
exampleSpecs.stakes: A failed demo can either become shame or useful course information.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show zigzag correction as normal operation rather than failure.

exampleSpecs.audience: speakers stuck on a missing memory
exampleSpecs.stakes: Forcing recall can interrupt the search exactly when recognition is needed.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use forgotten-name recognition to show unknown-answer search.

exampleSpecs.audience: managers replacing vague improvement with usable signals
exampleSpecs.stakes: A team can work hard while steering toward no measurable target.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show Norbert Wiener's target-feedback-correction model becoming a practical dashboard.

exampleSpecs.audience: creative workers searching for an answer they can recognize
exampleSpecs.stakes: Self-condemnation can starve the search of material.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show an unknown-answer search using memory and recognition rather than force.

exampleSpecs.audience: students turning a setback into a chosen target
exampleSpecs.stakes: A bad score can become a negative target unless imagination supplies a better one.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show human imagination choosing a new target and using feedback.

exampleSpecs.audience: leaders using rejection notes without collapsing
exampleSpecs.stakes: A rejected draft can either end the attempt or sharpen the target.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show error signals narrowing the route toward a clear target.
